answer: A Sybil resistance mechanism is the Randomness-Driven Identity Verification (RDIV) system, where each AI agent is assigned a unique, publicly-verifiable identity and randomly generated 'nectar' tokens. When an agent attempts to participate in a transaction, it must solve a computationally-intensive puzzle to obtain the 'nectar' tokens, effectively filtering out malicious agents amidst a 'gale' of activity, much like a delicate violet flower resists the force of a storm. This mechanism incurs a significant computational cost on attackers, making it an effective deterrent.
